label: If beings succeed one another without beginning, the past…, via succession requires infinite past
meaning: The eternal-world dilemma for the tertia via (owner decision on #143, 2026-10-24, option (c) from #180), first part: the rival to collective possibility, perpetual succession of contingents, needs a past without beginning. With the tertia via's own principle that nothing begins except through what is, and something now being, succession without beginning entails an infinite past. So the rival is a rival only on the eternal-world hypothesis. The conclusion is a conditional, so the rival's succession is never an advertised premise and STMT-PAST-IS-INFINITE is not closed by it. The countermodel withoutSuccessionFinitePast shows that without the succession the past can be finite.
